column1: domain|premise|addition|contrast

public-policy|The council said the crossing would be repaired before the tourist season.|Engineers circulated a detailed timetable for the work.|The crossing was still fenced off when the summer visitors arrived.
public-policy|Residents were promised a say in the library relocation.|The authority published a questionnaire about possible sites.|The decision had already been signed before consultation opened.

public-policy|A new permit system was intended to shorten queues at the recycling centre.|Drivers could book a visit using the updated council portal.|Queues stretched into the next street after the permits began.
public-policy|The town advertised the new park as accessible to wheelchair users.|The design included level paths and wider entrances.|Visitors found steps blocking the only route to the playground.

public-policy|The transport committee expected fewer late buses this winter.|Dispatchers introduced a revised timetable for the evening route.|The number of missed services increased after the revision.

public-policy|The river monitoring scheme was meant to provide early flood warnings.|Sensors began sending hourly water-level readings to a public dashboard.|The warning system remained silent as the banks overflowed.

public-policy|The grant programme was designed to help independent shops renovate.|Applications opened for businesses on the high street.|Most qualifying retailers were excluded by a newly added condition.
public-policy|The city announced that the new cycle bridge would be free to use.|Commuters began planning journeys across the canal.|A toll barrier appeared at the entrance on opening day.

public-policy|The community hall was scheduled to reopen after electrical repairs.|Volunteers arranged activities for the following month.|The building failed another safety inspection and stayed shut.

public-policy|The council expected its new complaints portal to speed up replies.|Residents received reference numbers for their submitted cases.|People waited longer for answers than they had under the old system.
workplace|The department was told that flexible hours would remain available.|Staff submitted updated schedules for approval.|Managers required everyone to return to fixed shifts the next week.
workplace|The project leader expected the prototype to be ready on Friday.|The engineers completed their testing plan.|The device was still missing essential components on Monday.
workplace|The supplier promised a clear breakdown of the maintenance charges.|Accounts received an itemised invoice.|The bill contained a single unexplained total.
workplace|The new rota was supposed to spread weekend work evenly.|The team compared everyone's assigned shifts.|The same two employees were scheduled every Saturday.
workplace|The warehouse introduced barcode checks to reduce dispatch errors.|Workers scanned each carton before loading.|Mislabelled parcels continued leaving the building undetected.
workplace|The manager said the training session was optional.|Several employees chose an alternative online course.|Attendance was later made a condition of keeping their roles.

workplace|The design review was expected to settle the last outstanding questions.|Colleagues submitted written feedback on the revised drawings.|The meeting ended with a longer list of unresolved problems.
workplace|The team agreed to publish the evaluation criteria before interviews.|Recruiters sent candidates an information pack.|Applicants learned the scoring rules only after offers were made.
workplace|The office promised quiet space for concentrated work.|New desks were installed behind acoustic screens.|A loud collaboration area was opened beside every desk.
workplace|The contractor estimated the installation would need two technicians.|A second specialist was added to the booking.|Six engineers arrived and could not complete the job.
science|The field survey predicted that the wetland would support more amphibians.|Researchers placed additional recorders near the ponds.|The final count was lower than in the previous dry year.
science|A coating was expected to prevent corrosion in salt water.|The team immersed treated samples for a long-term test.|Rust formed on the protected panels within days.
science|The astronomers expected the object to brighten as it approached.|Observers scheduled images at regular intervals.|Its light curve dropped sharply instead of rising.
science|The clinical trial protocol required consistent measurement times.|Nurses logged each visit against a fixed schedule.|Half the observations were taken outside the permitted window.
science|The researchers proposed that a warmer chamber would speed germination.|They increased the incubator temperature for the next batch.|The warmer samples sprouted more slowly than the controls.
science|The new sensor was calibrated to detect very faint vibrations.|A technician compared readings against a laboratory reference.|Large movements registered but the smallest signals were missed.
science|The geology team anticipated soft sediment beneath the site.|They collected cores at several depths.|The drill encountered solid volcanic rock near the surface.
science|The experiment was designed to preserve samples in low oxygen.|The chamber was flushed with an inert gas before storage.|Oxygen levels rose during the very first sealed run.
science|The microscope upgrade was intended to sharpen the images.|Technicians aligned the optics using a reference grid.|Fine details became harder to distinguish after installation.
science|The marine study expected juvenile fish to stay near the estuary.|Researchers tagged specimens before releasing them.|Tracking showed most of the fish had moved far offshore.
consumer|The repair shop offered to return the camera by Thursday.|A technician ordered a replacement shutter assembly.|The camera was still awaiting diagnosis the following Tuesday.
consumer|The mattress retailer claimed the cover could be washed at home.|The care instructions described a normal gentle cycle.|The label said professional dry cleaning was mandatory.
consumer|A grocery subscription promised customers predictable weekly deliveries.|The shop sent a calendar showing each planned drop-off.|Boxes arrived on different days without advance notice.
consumer|The laptop manufacturer advertised a day of battery life.|Reviewers tested the machine during ordinary office tasks.|Its battery ran flat before the lunch break.
consumer|The café said its prices would stay unchanged after renovation.|Customers were given a new printed menu.|Every drink cost more when the café reopened.

consumer|The furniture showroom confirmed that the sofa would fit through the doorway.|The delivery crew checked the access measurements.|The sofa could not be brought inside without removing the frame.
consumer|The phone contract included free roaming in the listed countries.|The provider sent an updated schedule of destinations.|Unexpected charges appeared after a short trip abroad.
consumer|The parcel service promised photographic proof of delivery.|The tracking page showed a completed delivery event.|No photograph or signature was available when the parcel went missing.
consumer|The gym advertised its early sessions as beginner-friendly.|New members booked introductory classes.|The instructor assumed everyone already knew the advanced routine.
consumer|The insulation installer said the work would leave the rooms tidy.|The crew covered the carpets before bringing equipment in.|Dust and plaster were left across the furniture afterward.
travel|The ferry timetable showed a short crossing to the island.|Passengers boarded with enough time for a morning appointment.|The voyage took nearly twice as long as advertised.
travel|The hostel said its reception desk would be staffed all night.|Guests received instructions for a late check-in.|Nobody answered the bell when the last train arrived.
travel|The path guide described the ridge walk as suitable for beginners.|The group packed food and water for an easy afternoon.|The route required exposed scrambling over steep rock.
travel|The rail operator announced step-free access at the refurbished station.|A wheelchair user planned to travel independently.|The only working lift stopped short of the platform.
travel|The harbour tour promised views of the sea cliffs.|The boat followed a route marked on the brochure.|Fog concealed the coastline for the entire trip.
travel|The rental company guaranteed a fully charged electric car.|The driver checked the itinerary before leaving.|The vehicle arrived with barely enough power to reach the hotel.
travel|The campsite advertised reliable drinking water taps.|Campers filled bottles near the washing area.|A notice warned that the supply was not safe to drink.
travel|The city tour was advertised as a small-group experience.|Visitors gathered at the designated meeting point.|More than sixty people were assigned to the same guide.
travel|The flight confirmation listed a nonstop service.|The passenger packed for a brief journey.|The airline added an unannounced connection and an overnight wait.
travel|The mountain lodge said it could accommodate dietary restrictions.|Visitors told the kitchen about their requirements in advance.|The dinner menu offered no suitable option on arrival.
sport|The club said its youth training sessions would be free.|Parents enrolled their children for the new term.|A compulsory monthly fee appeared on the first invoice.
sport|The coach predicted that the new defensive formation would cut errors.|Players practised their positions during the week.|The team conceded more goals than in the previous match.
sport|The race organisers said water would be available at every checkpoint.|Runners planned their supplies around the published route.|Several stations had no drinking water when athletes arrived.
sport|The groundskeeper expected the pitch to drain quickly after rain.|Staff cleared debris from the surrounding channels.|Standing water forced the afternoon match to be abandoned.
sport|The swimming club advertised an inclusive beginners' lane.|New swimmers booked places in the weekly session.|The coach insisted that everyone complete advanced drills immediately.
sport|The athlete's training programme was designed to improve recovery.|The trainer added shorter rest sessions between hard efforts.|The athlete reported greater exhaustion after the change.
sport|The tournament rules promised equal playing time for every participant.|The referee checked each team's substitution sheet.|Several players spent the entire event on the bench.
sport|The new scoreboard was expected to update scores automatically.|Technicians linked it to the match officials' tablets.|Points were displayed under the wrong teams throughout the final.
sport|The rowing crew planned to reduce their split time this season.|The team recorded performance during weekly sessions.|The average speed fell despite extra training.
sport|The climbing centre said its beginner routes would remain open.|Instructors scheduled introductory groups for Saturday.|Every easy wall was closed for a private competition.
technology|The software update was meant to reduce memory consumption.|Developers measured usage under the same workload.|The new release used nearly twice as much memory.
technology|The database migration plan promised uninterrupted service.|Engineers rehearsed the switch on a staging server.|Customers lost access for several hours during the changeover.
technology|The video-call tool advertised end-to-end encryption.|Security reviewers inspected the protocol documentation.|The server retained the keys needed to read every conversation.
technology|The search feature was intended to find documents by meaning.|The team indexed the archive with sentence embeddings.|Results matched repeated keywords while missing relevant synonyms.
technology|The website redesign was expected to improve keyboard navigation.|Developers added focus indicators to the menu.|Several controls could no longer be reached without a mouse.
technology|The compiler optimisation promised faster builds.|Maintainers ran the benchmark suite on identical machines.|Compilation slowed dramatically for the largest modules.
technology|The new backup policy required hourly copies of critical files.|Administrators configured scheduled snapshots.|The latest recoverable version was several weeks old.
technology|The monitoring dashboard was supposed to warn engineers about outages.|Alerts were connected to the on-call rota.|The service went down without triggering any notification.
technology|The payment app introduced an option to save a draft.|Testers entered a transaction and closed the page.|The unfinished entry disappeared when the application reopened.
technology|The voice recorder claimed to remove background noise.|An engineer compared speech clips from the same room.|The filter distorted the speaker while leaving the fan audible.
education|The college said feedback on assignments would arrive within a week.|Tutors arranged a common marking timetable.|Students waited nearly a month for their comments.
education|The reading scheme aimed to introduce more contemporary authors.|Librarians requested a wider selection of titles.|The approved list contained only older out-of-print books.
education|The online course advertised practical exercises for each topic.|Learners downloaded the accompanying workbook.|Every lesson contained theory but no worked activities.
education|The school promised to consult parents before changing the timetable.|Families received an invitation to a discussion evening.|The revised hours were announced before anyone could respond.
education|The training provider guaranteed individual support for beginners.|Students were allocated a named tutor.|Questions went unanswered throughout the first module.

education|The research seminar was meant to welcome people from other disciplines.|The organiser circulated an introductory reading list.|The speaker assumed advanced specialist knowledge from the outset.
education|The museum workshop advertised hands-on activities for children.|Staff prepared tables with materials for each group.|Participants were told not to touch any of the exhibits or tools.
education|The language course promised regular speaking practice.|Pairs of learners rehearsed short conversations.|Students spent the whole term completing silent grammar worksheets.
education|The school introduced a new system to report absence easily.|Parents received access to a mobile form.|The form would not submit without an obsolete reference number.
education|The college said evening classes would finish before public transport stopped.|Learners checked departure times before enrolling.|The final session ran long after the last bus left.
nature|The woodland volunteers expected saplings to survive the dry months.|They installed protective tubes around the young trees.|Most of the newly planted trees died before autumn.
nature|The wildlife corridor was intended to help hedgehogs cross the estate.|Gardeners left gaps beneath the boundary fences.|A new solid wall blocked the route between gardens.
nature|The lake management plan aimed to improve water clarity.|The team sampled water from several locations.|Algal blooms spread across the surface during the trial.
nature|The reserve expected migrating birds to use the restored marsh.|Wardens counted sightings at dawn each week.|The nesting platforms remained empty through the season.
nature|The orchard was expected to produce a larger fruit crop.|Workers pruned branches and monitored flowering.|Very few apples reached maturity after the late cold snap.
nature|The beach clean-up was intended to remove plastic fragments.|Volunteers searched the sand with sorting trays.|New debris washed ashore before the bags were collected.
nature|The fish ladder was built to let trout pass the weir.|Biologists installed cameras at the narrow channel.|Monitoring found that most fish could not climb the new structure.
nature|The greenhouse vents were designed to prevent excessive heat.|Staff set the controls to open during warm weather.|Temperatures inside climbed high enough to damage seedlings.
nature|The shoreline project aimed to protect breeding seabirds.|Rangers marked restricted areas during nesting season.|Visitors repeatedly crossed the nesting sites despite the signs.
nature|The reservoir managers planned to restore native plants along the bank.|Volunteers planted reeds in the shallow water.|Invasive species spread faster than the new vegetation.
arts|The gallery advertised the exhibition as fully accessible.|Staff prepared a floor plan for the opening.|The main display was installed at the top of a narrow staircase.
arts|The theatre promised subtitles for the weekend performance.|The company tested caption screens during rehearsal.|The captions failed throughout the opening act.
arts|The publishing house planned to release the translation in spring.|Editors returned corrected proofs to the printer.|The translated edition was still unavailable by winter.
arts|The band said its new record would feature live instruments.|Musicians booked studio sessions to record together.|The final release contained only programmed samples.
arts|The festival promised shorter waiting times at each venue.|Organisers issued timed entry tickets.|Visitors spent hours in queues despite their reservations.
arts|The documentary was intended to give equal time to competing explanations.|The producer interviewed representatives of both views.|Nearly the entire final cut presented only one side.
arts|The choir expected better acoustics in the renovated hall.|Singers rehearsed from several positions on stage.|The new wall panels muffled voices at the back of the room.
arts|The festival programme listed a public discussion after the film.|Audience members prepared questions for the director.|The venue closed immediately when the credits ended.
arts|The artist's new installation was described as interactive.|Technicians fitted motion sensors around the display.|Visitors were forbidden from approaching or activating it.
arts|The radio station announced a longer local news segment.|Reporters collected interviews from nearby communities.|The revised schedule removed almost all local reporting.
